title: Astronomers warn SpaceX’s million AI satellites threaten research
summary:
Astronomy organizations warn that SpaceX’s proposed network of AI-computing satellites could disrupt scientific observations after the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) authorized up to 1 million Starmind spacecraft on Nov. 25. The American Astronomical Society said the satellites could be brighter and more numerous than existing objects, remain visible longer, and produce radio emissions and waste heat that could affect sensitive instruments [cnn.com#1][wlbt.com#1].

Starmind would use computing hardware on solar-powered satellites to process AI workloads in orbit, then send results to Earth through SpaceX’s satellite network. The plan aims to meet AI’s demand for more computing capacity, but experts cite unresolved challenges in removing heat in a vacuum and moving large volumes of data. SpaceX warned in a regulatory filing that the technologies were unproven and might not be commercially viable [aerospaceglobalnews.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][cnn.com#1].

A European Southern Observatory simulation estimated that satellite trails could obscure up to 28% of images captured by its Very Large Telescope in Chile under specified conditions, even if SpaceX substantially dims its satellites [zmescience.com#1]. The FCC authorization sets deployment deadlines through 2040, requiring an operational satellite by November 2033 [cnn.com#1][independent.co.uk#1].

talking_points: Environmental risks: Launches and reentries could pollute the atmosphere, while in-orbit collisions could create debris clouds that threaten other satellites [wlbt.com#1].
Collision risks: SpaceX can maneuver functioning satellites to avoid potential collisions, but failed satellites cannot maneuver and could pose a danger in orbit [theconversation.com#1].
Other projects: Blue Origin has asked the FCC to approve up to 51,600 satellites for Project Sunrise [techspot.com#1].
Orbit design: The FCC order places the satellites in orbital shells between 500 and 1,002 kilometers, with 30-degree and sun-synchronous inclinations [spaceflightnow.com#1].
Strategic control: An expert raised concerns that one entity would control a capability of this scale and that it could become a target for malicious actors [scimex.org#1].

Earth-side pressure: A Data Center Watch tally cited by ZME Science said local opposition delayed or derailed at least 120 U.S. data-center projects worth $198 billion in the first half of 2026 [zmescience.com#1].

Observatory disruption: A simulation by European Southern Observatory astronomer Olivier Hainaut estimated that hundreds or thousands of satellites could be visible at once, rivaling the number of stars visible under pristine conditions [zmescience.com#1].
Launch dependency: SpaceX’s deployment plan depends heavily on lower launch costs from Starship, its reusable next-generation rocket, which is still under development [independent.co.uk#1].
Instrument interference: The American Astronomical Society warned that radio emissions and infrared waste heat from the satellites could threaten sensitive instruments used in astronomy [ksl.com#1].
Communications: FCC approval allows radio-frequency links as a backup for telemetry, tracking and command if the satellites’ optical links fail [spaceflightnow.com#1].

Orbital disposal condition: The FCC approved SpaceX’s debris plan only for satellites below 600 kilometers; the company must submit a final disposal plan before deploying satellites in higher orbits [universemagazine.com#1].
Visible objects: Astronomer Michael Brown says each proposed satellite would be about 75 metres wide and brighter than any star in the early evening [theconversation.com#1].
Satellite scale: SpaceX’s proposed AI1 spacecraft is designed with a wingspan of nearly 230 feet [techspot.com#1].
Existing traffic: About 17,000 satellites were already in orbit when the FCC approved the plan [aaj.tv#1][ksl.com#1].

perspectives.text: American Astronomical Society: The society said the FCC’s approval could compromise decades of federal investment in astronomy and people’s ability to study the night sky; it had urged the agency to reject the application [cnn.com#1][wlbt.com#1].

European Southern Observatory: Director General Andreas Kaufer called for international mechanisms to assess satellite projects whose effects cross national borders, citing the observatory’s technical analysis of the proposed constellation [LeonardDavid.com#1].

Federal Communications Commission: The commission said it would not impose additional protections for optical astronomy, which it considers outside its radio-frequency remit, and accepted SpaceX’s commitment to coordinate with the National Science Foundation [universemagazine.com#1].

Amazon Leo: Amazon’s satellite unit challenged the project’s feasibility, describing it as “an ambitious dream, not a real plan,” and argued SpaceX was unlikely to deploy the full fleet [bbc.co.uk#1][independent.co.uk#1].
American Astronomical Society: The society had urged the FCC to deny SpaceX’s application before the authorization [npr.org#1].
Adam Becker, astrophysicist and author: Becker called the proposal a fantasy and said it would not happen [npr.org#1].
Sir Martin Sweeting, Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd: Sweeting said the concept may be technically feasible but questioned whether it makes sense at scale [bbc.co.uk#1].

Federal Communications Commission: The FCC said approval serves the public interest by allowing SpaceX to pioneer technology intended to advance U.S. leadership in space and artificial intelligence [ahram.org.eg#1].
Amazon: The rival company criticized Starmind as “a lofty ambition rather than a real plan” [bbc.co.uk#1].
Federal Communications Commission: The commission said deploying the satellites serves the public interest, despite public comments and petitions asking it to deny SpaceX’s request [pbs.org#1].
SpaceX: The company told the FCC that near-constant solar power and low operating costs could reduce the environmental impact of computing compared with terrestrial data centers [ksl.com#1].

technical_details: Thermal radiation: In orbit, air cannot carry heat away from processors; the proposed satellites would have to release waste heat as infrared radiation through radiators [aerospaceglobalnews.com#1][techgenyz.com#1].

Hardware reliability: Unlike terrestrial servers, orbital processors are difficult to repair or replace. Technical challenges outlined for Starmind include the need for radiation protection and fault-tolerant hardware [techgenyz.com#1].

Distributed computing clusters: SpaceX executive Michael Nicholls described clusters of roughly 10 satellites linked at about 10 terabits per second, with connections to Starlink and the wider constellation [spaceflightnow.com#1].

Compute payload: SpaceX’s proposed payload is rated for roughly 175 kilowatts of average computing power and up to 250 kilowatts at peak; these are design specifications, not demonstrated operating results [techgenyz.com#1].
Payload power: SpaceX’s planned AI1 satellite is rated to provide its computing hardware with 120 kilowatts of sustained power and 150 kilowatts at peak [techspot.com#1].
Instrument risks: The American Astronomical Society also cited radio emissions and waste heat as threats to sensitive instruments used in astronomy research [ksl.com#1].
scientific_significance: Disposal requirements: The FCC has not approved SpaceX’s proposal to send retired satellites into solar orbit and requires a final debris plan before deployment above 600 kilometers [techspot.com#1].

Atmospheric uncertainty: Scientists have raised concerns that repeated satellite burn-ups could deposit metals in the upper atmosphere, including aluminium compounds that researchers have linked to ozone destruction. The projected scale depends on the satellites’ eventual operating lifespan and replacement rate [theconversation.com#1][scimex.org#1].
Hardware resilience: Experts identify processors’ ability to withstand space radiation and micrometeorite impacts as unresolved obstacles [dawn.com#1].
Proposed limit: Hainaut recommended limiting the total satellite population to approximately 100,000 sufficiently dim satellites to protect astronomical observations [zmescience.com#1].
Environmental effects: Critics also cited atmospheric pollution from satellite launches and reentries as a potential concern [npr.org#1].

suggested_qna.question: Does approval mean SpaceX will launch all one million satellites?
suggested_qna.answer: Not necessarily. Operators may request approval for more satellites than they intend to deploy. SpaceX sought clearance for 42,000 Starlink satellites and has put just over 11,000 in orbit [aaj.tv#1].

suggested_qna.question: What disposal review remains before some Starmind satellites can be deployed?
suggested_qna.answer: The FCC deferred SpaceX’s proposal to place retired satellites in solar orbit and requires a final debris plan before deployment above 600 kilometers [techspot.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Why could the highest satellite orbits raise disposal concerns?
suggested_qna.answer: The FCC approved disposal planning for satellites below 600 kilometers but deferred deployment in higher orbits until SpaceX submits a final disposal plan. The company had not supplied enough information for the FCC to assess its proposed methods [universemagazine.com#1].

historical_background: Satellite operators sometimes seek approval for more satellites than they ultimately intend to deploy to preserve flexibility in their network designs. SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites, while just over 11,000 are now in orbit [independent.co.uk#1][aaj.tv#1].

title: Anthropic co-founders disclosed $560 million in pre-IPO share sales
summary:
Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei, the chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, the company’s president and board chair, each sold 3.3784 million shares at the $83 initial public offering price, worth about $560 million combined, according to filings cited by BigGo [biggo.com#1]. Shares in the Claude developer closed at $82.79 on Nov. 25, below the offer price five trading sessions after its record $81.3 billion IPO [tradingview.com#1][trefis.com#1].

Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, up from $1.38 billion a year earlier, while the company recorded a $567 million operating loss [fool.com#3]. Computing and infrastructure expenses rose $4.3 billion in the quarter as revenue increased $5.4 billion from the previous quarter [fool.com#3].

The company has roughly $900 billion in long-term computing and infrastructure commitments and faces a series of share lockup expirations. Up to 303 million shares could become eligible for sale on Dec. 15, and Anthropic is expected to release its first results as a public company early next year [fool.com#3][trefis.com#1][biggo.com#1].
quote: It seems that these companies are trying to one-up each other on the amount of money that they're spending, but you have to show that it's worth it, and that's where Wall Street is saying 'I don't know'
quote_author: Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management
talking_points: Customer growth: The number of Anthropic customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue rose from more than 950 to over 11,900 in a year; more than 1,900 customers were spending at least $1 million annually by the third quarter [fool.com#3].

Usage-based sales: About 79% of Anthropic’s revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came from usage-based charges, leaving sales exposed if customers reduce token consumption or switch to cheaper models [fool.com#3].

Discount pressure: Price cuts and customer discounts introduced in the second and third quarters reduced revenue by about $600 million, as Anthropic competed with ChatGPT, Gemini and other models [fool.com#3][eleconomista.com.mx#1].
IPO float: About 11% of Anthropic’s shares were freely tradable at listing, compared with less than 5% in SpaceX’s IPO, according to BigGo’s comparison [biggo.com#1].
Sector strain: The Nov. 26 selloff also hit major AI-linked firms: Nvidia fell 8.5%, while CoreWeave and Nebius each dropped more than 10% [zawya.com#1].

perspectives.text: Chris Beauchamp, IG Group’s chief market analyst, said attention after an IPO typically shifts from hype to scrutiny of financial performance, growth prospects and valuation [biggo.com#1].

Tom Hulick, chief executive of Strategy Asset Managers, said investors should wait for reported results to confirm performance, describing Anthropic as a test case for the AI capital-spending cycle [biggo.com#1].

industry_impact: Cloud and chip suppliers: Anthropic’s infrastructure relies on providers including Amazon, Google and Microsoft for computing capacity and on Nvidia and AMD for chips, while some of those firms also compete in AI or hold investments in the company [eleconomista.com.mx#1].

AI infrastructure finance: CoreWeave’s 2031 bond yield approached 18% as its price fell near record lows, while credit-default swap spreads for Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave reached records [zawya.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What will investors look for in Anthropic’s first public-company earnings report?
suggested_qna.answer: They will be watching whether sales are running above the $68 billion annualized pace recorded in September and whether revenue growth can outpace computing costs [foreignpolicyjournal.com#1][tradingview.com#1].

historical_background: Nine large U.S. technology listings that fell at least 10% below their first-day closing price within six sessions later fell at least 33.9% from that close within two years [trefis.com#1]. Only three of those nine were above their first-day close after one year, and the median return was a loss of 23.9% [trefis.com#1]. The comparison is limited: the cases span different market periods, and Anthropic’s roughly $1.11 trillion valuation at the time exceeded those of the other companies at listing [trefis.com#1].
business_angle: Anthropic’s adjusted operating margin fell from 19% in the second quarter to 15% in the third, mainly due to $5 billion in costs associated with short-term computing-capacity deals [fool.com#3].

The company reported net revenue retention of about 900% at the end of September, but the calculation includes customers who generated as little as $1 in revenue in the prior-year quarter [fool.com#3].
Separate from scheduled lockup expirations, future secondary share issuances could reduce existing shareholders’ ownership stakes [fool.com#3].

title: SAP targets product and engineering teams in AI overhaul
summary:
SAP has asked teams in product development, engineering and sales to identify potential reductions as it reorganizes its enterprise software business around artificial intelligence. People familiar with the discussions said earlier attempts to introduce AI products faced problems [bloomberg.com#1][thehindubusinessline.com#1]. The plan under consideration would eliminate at least 10,000 jobs, but the final figure could change after labor negotiations [bloomberg.com#1][reuters.com#1].

At a May user conference, SAP introduced Joule Work, an interface intended to give employees a single point of access to its applications, along with Joule Assistants and Industry AI for sector-specific workflows [siliconangle.com#1]. SAP said its assistants would use more than 200 subagents to automate repetitive business tasks [siliconangle.com#1].

SAP has not confirmed the proposed cuts [bloomberg.com#1]. In the United States, employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, about 20% of the total, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas [cnbc.com#1]. SAP is expected to provide more detail with its full-year results in January [freepressjournal.in#1].
quote: Companies are spending billions of dollars on AI infrastructure, software and talent. At the same time, many are trimming roles viewed as overlapping, manual or less critical to future growth
quote_author: Krishna Iyer, corporate governance expert
talking_points: AI investments: SAP completed four acquisitions in 2026—Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf—and made strategic investments in AI-focused firms Parloa, n8n and Conduct [cnbc.com#1].
Previous overhaul: SAP’s 2024 restructuring relied mainly on voluntary departures and retraining; hiring for new roles kept overall headcount relatively flat [bworldonline.com#1].

German protections: An agreement negotiated by SAP’s German employee representatives protects employment through 2028 and provides alternative roles, training and preserved salary levels for affected employees [calcalistech.com#1].

Leadership changes: Two of SAP’s six executive board members are due to leave in March. Chief Executive Christian Klein took over most of product lead Muhammad Alam’s duties, while sales chief Thomas Saueressig plans to leave for Ionos [bworldonline.com#1].

perspectives.text: SAP: The company said it regularly reviews its organization to keep it aligned with its strategy and customer needs. It declined to confirm whether cuts are planned [bloomberg.com#1].

title: AI shopping assistants reshape Black Friday as scams and errors rise
summary:
Consumers are using artificial intelligence chatbots to compare prices and find gift ideas, while newer AI agents can browse stores, track deliveries and make purchases. The U.S. National Retail Federation says 59% of consumers plan to use AI for holiday shopping; Black Friday is Nov. 27, followed by Cyber Monday on Nov. 30 [gpb.org#1][tovima.gr#1]. In Australia, a separate survey found one in four shoppers planned to use an AI chatbot for research, and 72% of that group said it would be their first time [theconversation.com#1].

Chatbots can invent products or prices, recommend unsuitable items and expose data shared to personalize results. Visa testing found AI models failed to recommend a product matching a customer’s needs in 42% of test runs, while cybersecurity experts warn that malicious website instructions can manipulate agents with access to email or payment details [gpb.org#1][perthnow.com.au#1].

Retailers are also using AI to set discounts and influence which products shoppers see. title: Governments and AI leaders press for human oversight as safety rules diverge
summary:
Governments and technology leaders are pursuing AI safety measures ranging from voluntary international commitments to proposed inspections and mandatory incident reporting. The Paris Call, signed Nov. 9 by governments, AI companies and civil-society groups, is nonbinding, while the U.S. administration has favored industry-led safeguards and Congress has yet to pass proposed federal requirements [cyberpeace.org#1][pymnts.com#1]. California’s transparency law took effect in January 2026; New York’s RAISE Act is due to take effect in January 2027, and Japan’s government aims to submit legislation requiring reports of serious AI failures to its 2027 ordinary parliamentary session [pymnts.com#1][nikkei.com#2].

At a Nov. 23 United Nations summit in Barbados, Finland’s Transport and Communications Minister Lulu Ranne said human interests and governance should be central to AI development [telecompaper.com#1]. Experts at a Brookings Institution discussion urged the United States and China to cooperate on incident reporting, testing standards and researcher exchanges, even if their domestic regulations differ [chinadailyasia.com#1]. In Russia, President Vladimir Putin called for clear limits on what AI agents can do without human approval [tass.com#1].

AI safety expert Stuart Russell called for international standards and mandatory pre-release testing, while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that regulators should use existing laws unless they identify a specific gap [hindustantimes.com#1][yahoo.com#1]. Japan’s proposed bill would allow inspections when safeguards are inadequate and penalties of up to 100 million yen, according to Nikkei [nikkei.com#2].
quote: We need to establish the limits of authority for AI agents - that is, the steps they cannot take without human oversight and participation.
quote_author: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
talking_points: Paris commitments: The Paris Call includes commitments to independent validation, model fail-safes, ongoing risk assessments and faster sharing of information about serious incidents, but sets no deadlines [cyberpeace.org#1].
Signatory gaps: China, Google and Meta were not listed at the time described [cyberpeace.org#1].

Thailand’s legal gap: Technology law specialist Paiboon Amornpinyo said Thailand’s cybercrime, data-protection and cybersecurity laws were not designed for AI-driven attacks and called for an emergency decree while longer-term legislation is prepared [bangkokpost.com#1].
Regulatory comparison: Russell said China had implemented tougher AI regulations than the United States and Europe [hindustantimes.com#1].
Federal proposals: Congressional proposals include independent audits, incident reporting and pre-deployment evaluations, but none had become law [pymnts.com#1].

perspectives.text: Stuart Russell, University of California, Berkeley professor and AI expert: He warned that AI loss-of-control incidents already seen in cyberspace could eventually spill over into financial markets [hindustantimes.com#1].

Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive: Huang urged data-center builders to work more closely with nearby communities, including making facilities more attractive and locating them far enough away to avoid disturbing residents [yahoo.com#1].
Kyle Chan, Brookings Institution fellow: He said discussions on human control of military AI could offer a practical area for gradual U.S.-China progress [chinadailyasia.com#1].

Nobel Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes: Frydnes argued that accountability must remain with the people and governments that design, deploy and profit from AI, because a machine cannot answer to victims in court [rappler.com#1].

title: Nvidia pauses AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian markets
summary:
Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers containing its advanced artificial-intelligence chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. The duration is unclear. The report described the hold as a compliance step while Nvidia and its partners work through new U.S. export controls [ft.com#1][wsj.com#1][channelnewsasia.com#1].

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule on Nov. 16 that took effect Nov. 19. It requires licenses for covered advanced-chip shipments to the four countries and Brazil. It also targets overseas data centers that provide substantial computing capacity to companies in China and other restricted jurisdictions. Existing providers serving those customers have 90 days to apply for licenses to continue those services [firstpost.com#1][techrepublic.com#1][investingnews.com#1].

The controls affect projects built around leasing Nvidia-powered computing to Chinese customers. Singapore cloud provider Aolani had planned to serve ByteDance; lenders have stopped extending about $500 million in credit for the project, and ByteDance may abandon the arrangement. Nvidia booked $104 billion through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, a figure that also includes some Taiwan and China revenue [ft.com#1][cna.com.tw#1][siliconrepublic.com#1].
talking_points: Compute threshold: The rule requires a license when a data center supplies more than 12 million aggregate total processing performance units to covered customers; linked facilities count together [firstpost.com#1][investingnews.com#1][casrai.org#1].

U.S. carve-out: The destination-based licensing requirement does not apply to shipments for U.S.-headquartered companies or companies whose ultimate parent is U.S.-based, subject to reporting requirements [techrepublic.com#1][news18.com#1][casrai.org#1].

Regional investment: Malaysia approved RM123.5 billion in data-center and cloud investments across 86 projects from January through September 2026, although the number relying on affected shipments is unknown [techrepublic.com#1].

Credit exposure: Lenders are also taking longer to review a $6.6 billion loan sought by Bain Capital’s Bridge Data Centres for Malaysian facilities serving ByteDance, according to CoinDesk [coindesk.com#1].

perspectives.text: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the Commerce Department’s rule is intended to block indirect access to restricted computing, including through smuggling routes and remote use of third-country data centers [thestandard.co#1].

Malaysia’s trade ministry said Malaysia does not require a local permit to import AI chips and does not enforce other countries’ unilateral export controls, but expects local businesses to take those rules into account [news18.com#1].

Regional cloud providers: Cloud operators have complained that the 90-day licensing period began without clear application instructions, making it harder to demonstrate compliance [techspot.com#1][ft.com#1].

title: X adds first parental controls for teens after safety scrutiny
summary:
X introduced its first parental controls on Nov. 26 for users ages 13 to 17, giving parents and guardians tools to manage teens’ feeds, contacts and time spent on the social network [techcrunch.com#1][mashable.com#1][ndtv.com#1]. Teen accounts default to protected mode, which restricts sensitive media and blocks targeted advertising. Adults can set daily usage limits, approve new followers, filter words, limit recommendations to accounts the teen follows and control who can send direct messages [engadget.com#1][techjuice.pk#1].

Supervision requires consent from both the adult and the teen. Parents can see weekly usage and which accounts their teen has messaged one-on-one, but cannot read the messages, view search or viewing histories, log in to the teen’s account or post on their behalf. Teenagers can see every change made [pcmag.com#1][ndtv.com#1].

One adult can supervise up to five teen accounts, while each teen account can be linked to only one adult. Supervision ends automatically when the teen turns 18 [mashable.com#1][9to5mac.com#1].
quote: Parents want practical tools, and teens deserve room to grow. With Parental Controls on X, families can set the guardrails that fit their home, while teens keep ownership of their accounts and can see every change. Striking that balance is vital and what we set out to build.
quote_author: Michael O’Herlihy, head of safety at X
talking_points: Account linking: The parent starts setup in X’s settings and the teen completes it by scanning a QR code while logged into their account [firstpost.com#1][pcmag.com#1].
Age verification: X may verify a user’s age through a selfie check or identity document in some cases, but the platform has not specified when it will require either method [tweakers.net#1].
Safety testing: The Center for Countering Digital Hate said two UK accounts posing as 13-year-olds could find sexual acts and pornographic images and videos on X [digitaltrends.com#1].

Legal scrutiny: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general sued X and other Musk companies, alleging Grok helped spread non-consensual sexual images and child sexual abuse material [digitaltrends.com#1][pcmag.com#1].
Default account limits: Teen accounts are set so only approved followers can view posts and only accounts the teen follows can send direct messages [techjuice.pk#1].

perspectives.text: X: The company says its platform is not designed or promoted for children, but says it takes extra care with young people who use it [gizmodo.com#1][techcrunch.com#1].

Ofcom: The UK regulator’s investigation found that some age-gated pornography remained accessible to accounts not verified as belonging to adults. X subsequently changed its restrictions [digitaltrends.com#1].

title: Analysts say GTA VI needs PC release to expand beyond console market
summary:
Analysts estimate Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI sold 40.2 million to 47 million copies over its launch weekend, with several forecasting at least 50 million by year-end. The game, released Nov. 19, generated $3.79 billion on its first day, while Sony said more than 39 million people played it on PlayStation 5 during its first four days [gamesindustry.biz#1][eurogamer.net#1][secretmag.ru#1].

Analysts say console sales face a limited audience: Video-game market analyst Joost van Dreunen estimates about 137 million current-generation consoles are in use and says roughly one-quarter of that base bought the game before release. They identify a PC version, which has not been announced, as the main route to a larger market. Van Dreunen forecasts lifetime sales of 200 million to 250 million copies, while Enders Analysis’ Gareth Sutcliffe says reaching 100 million quickly would require more platforms [gamesindustry.biz#1].

Sony also reported 683 million hours played on PS5 from Nov. 19 through Nov. 22, an average of 17.4 hours per player. Near-term sales depend on holiday demand and console availability; analysts say Sony and Microsoft have limited ability to increase supply this quarter and in the first quarter [secretmag.ru#1][gamesindustry.biz#1].
quote: Take-Two positioned GTA 6 less as a game and more as a blockbuster entertainment event.
quote_author: Joost van Dreunen, video-game market analyst
talking_points: Streaming audience: Streams Charts counted more than 420 million hours of GTA VI viewing across platforms in its first seven days, nearly three times the previous record held by Valorant’s 2020 closed beta [eurogamer.net#1].

Physical sales: Despite being sold in a box without a disc, the game generated £32 million in UK physical-retail revenue in three days, marking the country’s largest physical launch since 2019 [nintendolife.com#1].

title: 1Password reports customer data theft; investigation continues
summary:
Password manager 1Password says an attacker used a compromised employee GitHub account to access private source code, insert malicious code into backend services and download customer administrative records. The company began investigating on Nov. 19 and disclosed the incident on Nov. 25. Its investigation, assisted by independent cybersecurity experts, continues [securityweek.com#1][helpnetsecurity.com#1][thelec.net#1].

The stolen records included customer names, sign-in email addresses, account identifiers, activity timestamps, public keys and authentication parameters, as well as tokens in some invitation and recovery emails. The attacker also copied private source code and accessed the company’s software build-and-deployment system, which may hold infrastructure credentials. 1Password says the attacker did not access customer vault contents, passwords, recovery keys or the keys protecting vaults [securityweek.com#1][thehackernews.com#1][itpro.com#1].

1Password says exposed invitation and recovery tokens cannot be used alone to access accounts and reports no evidence of account takeovers. It disabled the compromised account, revoked a stolen token, rotated potentially exposed credentials and restored clean versions of affected services. The company has not disclosed the number of affected customers or how the attacker first accessed the employee’s GitHub account. It advises customers to watch for phishing messages [helpnetsecurity.com#1][techradar.com#1][indianexpress.com#1].
quote: At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.
quote_author: 1Password
talking_points: Development controls: 1Password says it tightened protections for GitHub, its software build-and-deployment system and employee devices, and added tools to detect intrusions [thehackernews.com#1][helpnetsecurity.com#1].
Customer notifications: 1Password said it individually notified a small number of people with outstanding provisioning or recovery invitations [thehackernews.com#1][helpnetsecurity.com#1].
Company reach: 1Password serves millions of individual users and about 200,000 businesses, according to The Lec [thelec.net#1].

Phishing exposure: Names and email addresses linked to 1Password accounts could help scammers tailor fake recovery messages, a risk highlighted by the company and security coverage [engadget.com#1][itpro.com#1][techspot.com#1].

perspectives.text: 1Password: The company says the Secure Remote Password verifiers in the stolen records cannot authenticate users directly. Attempts to brute-force account passwords would also require Secret Keys, which 1Password says it does not store [securityweek.com#1].

Sarkis Darbinyan, IT lawyer and digital-rights expert: Darbinyan said customer metadata can reveal who uses a service and when they were active, a concern for journalists and activists. He identified phishing as the immediate concern [novayagazeta.eu#1].

title: Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian defense technicians
summary:
Two Italian technicians were killed when drones struck a Kuwaiti military facility on Thursday, Nov. 26, and falling debris injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, Kuwaiti and Italian officials said [bbc.com#1][cnn.com#1][al-monitor.com#1]. The men worked for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian unit of German defense contractor Rheinmetall, maintaining detection antennas for Kuwait’s Skyguard air-defense system [dw.com#1][upi.com#1]. Kuwait and Italy blamed Iran; Tehran denied responsibility. Iran’s armed forces said they had conducted no operation in the region, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi offered to join Kuwait and Italy in investigating the incident [ndtv.com#1][tass.com#1].

Kuwait said its forces detected and intercepted hostile drones, but the defense ministry did not identify the facility or describe the damage [cnn.com#1][perthnow.com.au#1]. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the drones were Iranian-made and noted that Iran-aligned armed groups also operate in the region [cnn.com#1]. Attacks on Gulf states hosting U.S. forces had resumed after a relative lull, while negotiations to end the U.S.-Iran war remained stalled [bbc.com#1][haaretz.com#1].

Kuwait condemned the attack as a violation of its sovereignty and said it reserved the right to take measures to defend its territory [arabnews.com#1]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged increased pressure on Tehran, while Araghchi proposed a joint investigation with Kuwait and Italy [ndtv.com#1][nournews.ir#2].
quote: The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war. We stand ready to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause of the incident.
quote_author: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
talking_points: Victims identified: Italian news agency ANSA identified the technicians as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36 [haaretz.com#1][arabnews.com#1].

Gulf attack scale: Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi told the U.N. Security Council in mid-November that Iran had launched more than 7,000 missiles and drones at member states since the regional conflict began [rudaw.net#1].

Shipping risks: Maritime analyst Noam Raydan said at least 26 attacks on commercial vessels had been reported in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters during November, including attacks on at least 10 very large crude carriers [rudaw.net#1].
Kuwait’s legal stance: Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry said the attack breached the U.N. Charter and invoked Article 51 as the basis for its right to defend its territory [arabnews.com#1].

perspectives.text: Kuwait’s government: The Foreign Ministry warned that the attack threatened regional stability and undermined diplomatic efforts to ease tensions [arabnews.com#1].

Iranian government: Armed Forces spokesman Abolfazl Shekarchi said the accusations served as a cover for U.S. and Israeli efforts to increase regional instability, without presenting evidence [tass.com#2][ndtv.com#1].
European Commission: President Ursula von der Leyen said Gulf security was also a matter of security for Europe [dw.com#1].

Bader Al-Saif: The Kuwait University assistant professor and Chatham House associate fellow argued that analysts should not overlook Tehran’s agency when assessing the renewed attacks [livemint.com#1].

title: Trump urges Putin to halt European aggression as Ukraine war intensifies
summary:
President Donald Trump said on Nov. 26 that he had urged Russian President Vladimir Putin during talks in China the previous week to pull back “all military aggression” across Europe. He said he hoped that could lead to a quick deal to end the war in Ukraine but did not specify which territories or actions he meant. His statement followed a Florida meeting with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, after which they called on Russia and Ukraine to avoid steps that could widen the war [france24.com#1][scmp.com#1][dw.com#1].

At their China meeting, Trump greeted Putin as a “friend,” worrying officials in Kyiv and European capitals. Russian strikes hit Kyiv overnight, wounding seven people, while Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, warned of another possible mass attack. European concern has also grown after missiles landed in Poland [scmp.com#1][aljazeera.com#1][time.com#1].

Washington has delayed a review of the U.S. military presence in Europe beyond its provisional Dec. 1 deadline while it assesses options and European offers to replace some U.S. capabilities. The review will go to Trump, but officials have not set a date for a decision [rferl.org#1].
quote: The biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other
quote_author: President Donald Trump
talking_points: Troop review: The review covers U.S. troop levels, bases and overflight rights; about 80,000 U.S. troops are stationed in Europe, and the Pentagon is preparing five options [rferl.org#1].
Baltic tensions: Estonia accused Russian security services of ordering an attempted arson attack on a defense company; Moscow denied involvement [time.com#1].

War’s reach: Ukraine said its drones struck Russian oil facilities and an airfield, while Ukraine’s prime minister said Russian attacks hit two foreign grain ships carrying more than 100,000 tonnes [aljazeera.com#1][timeslive.co.za#1].
EU financing: EU leaders debated a proposed €45 billion loan to meet Ukraine’s needs in 2027; European Council President António Costa said 24 member states supported it [aljazeera.com#1].
Territorial deadlock: Trump envoy Jared Kushner said territory in eastern Ukraine claimed by Moscow remained a sticking point in discussions [thehindu.com#1][ndtv.com#1].

title: EU leaders fail to agree on €1.78 trillion seven-year budget
summary:
European Union leaders ended a Brussels summit early on Nov. 26 without agreement on the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget, a proposed €1.78 trillion package already cut by about €204 billion from the European Commission’s initial plan. European Council President António Costa said governments remained divided over the budget’s total size, spending allocations and new sources of EU revenue. The second day of talks was cancelled [euronews.com#1][tass.com#2][tass.com#6].

Germany and other net contributors want deeper cuts and more spending on defense and competitiveness, while France, Italy and other governments focused on cohesion funding oppose reductions to farm support and regional development. The dispute also became linked to a proposed €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027: 24 member states backed it, Bulgaria said it would fund only the non-military portion, and Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia remained opposed [reuters.com#1][tass.com#7][theguardian.com#1].

Leaders are due to resume negotiations at a summit on Dec. 17-18, aiming to reach agreement by year-end. The budget requires unanimous approval, and French President Emmanuel Macron has warned that without a deal by Dec. 31, formal talks would have to wait until after France’s 2027 presidential election [reuters.com#1][bworldonline.com#2][eleconomista.es#1].
quote: Europe needs solid finances. We can’t and we mustn’t take on more debt.
quote_author: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
talking_points: Budget priorities: Agriculture and cohesion policy each account for about one-third of the EU budget, while the proposed package would devote roughly €740 billion to farmers and poorer regions [scmp.com#1][reuters.com#1].

Ukraine allocation: The proposed €45 billion loan divides into €20 billion for civilian needs and €25 billion for arms and ammunition; the 2028-2034 draft also includes up to €100 billion for Ukraine [dw.com#1][independent.ie#1].

New revenue: A proposed digital-services levy could raise €35 billion, but Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin said it conflicted with efforts to improve European competitiveness [ft.com#1][thejournal.ie#1].

ECB appointment: Leaders separately backed Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos, former Bank of Spain governor, to succeed Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president in February [euronews.com#3][eualive.net#1].
Pandemic debt: The current budget proposal includes €140 billion to repay borrowing undertaken during the pandemic [reuters.com#1].

perspectives.text: European Council President António Costa: Costa said the summit was a necessary step and stressed that the EU needed a new budget in place from Jan. 1, 2028.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and net-contributor governments: Merz threatened to block the budget unless all 27 members backed the separate Ukraine loan, arguing the bloc should share the cost of aid [straitstimes.com#1][theguardian.com#1].
French President Emmanuel Macron: Macron called the proposed reductions a strategic error, warning they could leave Europe lagging in investment behind China and the United States [sudouest.fr#1].

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin: Martin identified the Common Agricultural Policy as a priority, saying it is a key EU funding stream for Ireland’s agriculture and food industry [thejournal.ie#1].

title: New Zealand coalition loses majority; centrist party holds balance of power
summary:
New Zealand’s governing National-led coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the final count of the Nov. 7 election, leaving it with 65 seats in a 130-seat Parliament, one short of the number needed to govern without additional support. The centrist Opportunity Party, which won seven seats, now holds the balance of power. The opposition Labour-led bloc has 58 seats and cannot form a majority even with Opportunity’s support [theguardian.com#1][abc.net.au#1][dw.com#1].

The Electoral Commission’s count included 484,865 special votes cast overseas or outside voters’ electorates. National lost two seats compared with the preliminary tally; Labour gained two electorate seats and the Greens one. Prime Minister and National leader Christopher Luxon, who had ruled out working with Opportunity during the campaign, said formal talks would begin with his existing partners and Opportunity. Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong said her support depends on policy commitments and that she will not back a government with New Zealand First leader Winston Peters as foreign affairs minister [theguardian.com#1][abc.net.au#1][euronews.com#1].

Negotiations could extend into 2027. Luxon has warned that talks may be difficult, and failure to secure a governing or confidence-and-supply arrangement could lead to another election. A recount could still change the seat totals: applications are due by Dec. 3, and a recount could take a further five days [theguardian.com#1][straitstimes.com#1].
quote: Getting it right matters far more than getting it done quickly
quote_author: Christopher Luxon, New Zealand prime minister and National Party leader
talking_points: Vote shares: Labour received 29.88% of the party vote and National 28.35%, but National won more electorate seats; 2.8 million votes were cast [abc.com.py#1][newsday.com#1].

Policy conditions: Opportunity’s stated priorities also include supermarket competition, political-donation limits, a 10-year cross-party health plan and ending bottom-trawling [theguardian.com#1][perthnow.com.au#1].
Narrow margins: Labour won Wairarapa from National by 81 votes and Hamilton East by 173, while the Greens took Wellington Bays from Labour by 1,610 [theguardian.com#1].
Election readiness: Chief Electoral Officer Karl Le Quesne said the Electoral Commission is prepared to run another election if parties cannot form a government [abc.net.au#1].
Voter turnout: Turnout was 77.2%, down from 78.2% in the 2023 election [aa.com.tr#1].

perspectives.text: Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong: Wong said her party could support a confidence-and-supply arrangement or remain on the crossbenches, with its MPs backing key legislation and assessing other bills individually [interest.co.nz#1][newsday.com#1].
ACT Party leader David Seymour: Seymour said a government could be formed quickly if the coalition was willing to work with Opportunity “at some level” [straitstimes.com#1].

Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins: Hipkins said Labour was not in a position to negotiate to form a government and that he would decide on his own leadership after a government was formed [straitstimes.com#1][abc.net.au#1].
Political scientist Luke Oldfield: Oldfield said the governing parties and Opportunity were likely to reach a deal, making a second election unlikely [straitstimes.com#1].

title: Spain votes Sunday with far-right Vox poised for national government role
summary:
Spain votes on Nov. 29 in a snap parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s eight years in office and give far-right Vox its first role in a national government since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship ended in 1975. Pre-election polls put the conservative People’s Party (PP) near 31%, the Socialists (PSOE) around 29% to 30% and Vox at roughly 17% to 18%. The PP is expected to need Vox’s support to reach the 176 seats required for a majority in the 350-seat Congress [straitstimes.com#1][abcnews.com#2][aljazeera.com#1].

Sánchez called the early vote after parliament rejected housing measures on Oct. 2, amid anger over high rents and evictions. The campaign has also focused on corruption investigations involving people close to Sánchez, two fatal train crashes and migration, including the summer influx into the North African enclave of Ceuta [straitstimes.com#1][abcnews.com#1][europrospects.eu#1].

The PP and Vox have signaled changes to climate policy. Polling stations open at 9 a.m. local time and close at 8 p.m. If no bloc secures a majority, parties will have to negotiate support for a government [aljazeera.com#1][politico.eu#1][politico.eu#2].
quote: A government of the PP that includes Vox would not be just another government; it would mean an enormous step backwards. It would mean rolling back the clock 40, 50 years
quote_author: Pedro Sánchez, prime minister of Spain
talking_points: Youth support: Support for Vox has risen to 23.2% among voters aged 18 to 24, slightly above the Socialists’ 22%, according to Spain’s November polling [france24.com#4].

Housing pledges: PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has promised one million new homes over four years, while Sánchez has emphasized tighter housing-market regulation and restrictions on unauthorized tourist rentals [abcnews.com#1].

Rail scrutiny: After two deadly train crashes this year, Feijóo has pledged a rapid audit of the rail network if elected; the transport minister resigned after the second crash [abcnews.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].
Election mechanics: Voters choose party lists in 52 constituencies, and parties need at least 3% of a constituency’s vote to qualify for seats there [aljazeera.com#1].
Coalition tensions: The PP and Vox have governed together in four regions, where they have clashed over policy [letemps.ch#1][nzz.ch#1].

perspectives.text: Pedro Sánchez, prime minister of Spain: Sánchez has defended legal immigration, arguing that people who come to Spain bring economic and social benefits [abcnews.com#1].

title: Defence minister probes claim nurse was threatened over Poilievre photo
summary:
Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty says he is trying to resolve a dispute involving government contractor Calian Health after Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre alleged a nurse’s contract was at risk because she spoke with him at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright. Maureen Carpenter, who works at the Wainwright hospital under contract with Calian, met Poilievre after an Oct. 17 fire at the Alberta base that killed five soldiers and injured 39 people, 19 critically [winnipegfreepress.com#1][globalnews.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1].

Poilievre raised a point of privilege in the House of Commons on Wednesday, saying the alleged employment consequences interfered with his work as Carpenter’s MP. McGuinty said he asked his deputy minister to raise the matter with Calian but cannot intervene directly in a private contract. He has spoken with Carpenter’s brother, but not with Carpenter. Calian had not responded to media requests for comment. The House Speaker is expected to rule on Poilievre’s privilege claim [cbc.ca#1][nationalobserver.com#1][winnipegfreepress.com#1].
quote: It’s not right that a member of Parliament should not be able to speak to a constituent.
quote_author: David McGuinty, Canada’s defence minister
talking_points: Contract concerns: Poilievre said Carpenter was told she could face scrutiny from Calian’s legal department and that other expected work opportunities had disappeared; he said she appealed reprimands and sought an apology [nationalobserver.com#1][torontosun.com#1].
Meeting permission: Poilievre said Carpenter spoke with him on base with permission from the unit commander, and that he had permission from the base commander to visit [cbc.ca#1][torontosun.com#1].

Cross-party response: Liberal MP Kevin Lamoureux said he found the claims upsetting and recognized health workers’ service, while Bloc Québécois MP Gabriel Ste-Marie said his party would examine the matter [globalnews.ca#1][ledevoir.com#1].

perspectives.text: Pierre Poilievre, Conservative Party leader: He said Carpenter was told she violated Calian Health policy by meeting with her MP, but argued the company has no such rule and that meeting an MP is a basic Charter right [torontosun.com#1].

title: Doctors warn Wainwright fire injuries may require years of recovery
summary:
Nearly six weeks after a wind-driven grass fire burned soldiers during a training exercise at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, doctors say some face months or years of physical and psychological recovery [globalnews.ca#1][thestar.com#1][cbc.ca#1]. Five soldiers have died; as of Thursday, 19 injured soldiers remained in Alberta hospitals, seven in critical condition, while the military said 22 were still hospitalized across Canada [globalnews.ca#1][thestar.com#1].

Burn specialist Dr. Josh Wong said treatment for severe burns can involve repeated surgeries, rehabilitation and ongoing psychological support. The fire overwhelmed the Edmonton burn unit, and three investigations are examining how it started and why live-fire training continued as strong winds pushed flames across the base [cbc.ca#1][edmontonjournal.com#1]. Health officials say they will review the emergency response after addressing immediate treatment needs [globalnews.ca#1][thestar.com#1].
quote: Their care doesn’t end when they leave the ICU or even the hospital.
quote_author: Dr. Josh Wong, interim medical director of the Firefighters’ Burn Treatment Unit at the University of Alberta Hospital
talking_points: Capacity surge: The Edmonton burn unit admitted 20 critically injured soldiers in a short period—five times its specialized critical-care capacity—while already treating 15 other burn patients [globalnews.ca#1][thestar.com#1].

Provincial response: Alberta’s emergency response used 30 transport units—22 ground ambulances, six fixed-wing aircraft and two helicopters—to move patients, with transfers continuing until about 2 or 3 a.m. [edmontonjournal.com#1].
Staff support: Doctors say health-care workers and first responders may experience fatigue and psychological effects in the weeks and months after the emergency [globalnews.ca#1][cbc.ca#1].

Treatment network: Soldiers received treatment at Royal Alexandra, Foothills and Red Deer Regional hospitals, while specialized medical teams from Ontario and Manitoba came to help [edmontonjournal.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].

perspectives.text: Dr. Sayeh Zielke, interim chief executive officer of Acute Care Alberta, said Alberta’s health system passed a stress test by coordinating the mass-casualty response while continuing to care for other patients [thestar.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].

sources.name: The Canadian Press via The Toronto Star

perspectives.text: Dr. Josh Wong, a burn surgeon, warned that the psychological impact of burns can become more pronounced as patients recover and become more aware of their injuries [globalnews.ca#1][thestar.com#1].

title: Conservatives seek parliamentary testimony from Carney’s wife on ocean envoy role
summary:
Conservative MPs are seeking parliamentary testimony from Diana Fox Carney, the wife of Prime Minister Mark Carney, about her unpaid appointment as Canada’s ocean envoy, citing questions about her mandate, travel costs and possible lobbying. On Thursday, Conservative MP Jonathan Rowe tabled a motion at the House environment committee asking her to appear; Liberal MPs adjourned debate. Conservatives say five earlier attempts to bring her before the House fisheries committee were also blocked [cbc.ca#1][winnipegfreepress.com#1].

A mandate letter obtained by The Globe and Mail describes Fox Carney’s role as voluntary, time-limited and focused on helping convene the Our Ocean Conference in Halifax in spring 2027. The letter does not identify who she reports to or set a travel budget. Fisheries Minister Joanne Thompson said Fox Carney does not manage the government’s $1.2-billion ocean-protection fund. The House ethics commissioner said last month he saw no conflict in her hosting the conference, while the commissioner’s office said an unpaid appointee without a cabinet order generally would not qualify as a public office holder under conflict-of-interest rules [theglobeandmail.com#2][sootoday.com#1].
quote: If you're going to be traveling abroad and speaking on behalf of Canadians, you have to be answerable to Canadians.
quote_author: Branden Leslie, Conservative MP for Manitoba
talking_points: Pre-appointment priorities: A departmental briefing note said Fox Carney had expressed interest in ocean-conservation financing and announcements related to the Arctic and the High Seas Treaty, and that chairing the conference could advance those interests [theglobeandmail.com#2].
Conference funding: The federal budget allocates $8 million over two years for Fisheries and Oceans Canada to host the Halifax conference [theglobeandmail.com#2].

Pledge record: The Our Ocean Conference has generated 3,270 voluntary commitments worth a combined US$176.7 billion since 2014; Canada accounts for 100 commitments worth US$4.2 billion [theglobeandmail.com#2].

Lobbying rules: The Lobbying Commissioner’s office said lobbyists report communications with designated public office holders, and whether Fox Carney’s role meets the comparable-rank test requires a case-specific analysis [theglobeandmail.com#2].

perspectives.text: Conservative MP Jonathan Rowe argued that people with greater ocean expertise could have been appointed instead of the prime minister’s spouse [winnipegfreepress.com#1].

summary:

title: Floodwaters peak along parts of B.C. coast; central Island remains under warning
summary:
Floodwaters have peaked across much of Vancouver Island and British Columbia’s south coast, but river levels remain a serious concern on central Vancouver Island after days of rain, high tides and storm surge. The provincial River Forecast Centre issued a flood warning for central Island waterways, where rivers had reached their banks or were expected to overflow soon. Officials said eastern Vancouver Island remained under a flood watch and coastal flood warnings continued in many areas [thestar.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][timescolonist.com#1].

Courtenay declared a local emergency and ordered evacuations from several low-lying properties, including the Maple Pool campground, while the Regional District of Nanaimo ordered some Cedar residents to leave homes along the Nanaimo River [thestar.com#1][timescolonist.com#1]. Rain and wind warnings for the South Coast were lifted Thursday, but officials said rivers would need time to recede before advisories could be withdrawn. The Effingham Island weather station recorded 469 millimetres of rain in just over two days [thestar.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1].
quote: This water has nowhere to go.
quote_author: Jennifer Kowal, Environment Canada meteorologist
talking_points: Rapid snowmelt: The River Forecast Centre said large amounts of mountain snow were melting quickly at lower elevations and feeding already swollen waterways [thestar.com#1][nationalobserver.com#1].
Evacuation support: Nanaimo Search and Rescue went door to door in Cedar, while emergency support services opened a reception area at Cedar Community Centre [timescolonist.com#1].
Farm flooding: Jenny James said flooding at her family’s farm has worsened in recent years; the family has owned the land since 1981 [timescolonist.com#1].
Ferry disruption: BC Ferries cancelled two Thursday morning sailings between Tsawwassen and Swartz Bay because of storm conditions [nationalobserver.com#1].

title: OpenAI says model established theoretical speed limit for matrix multiplication
summary:
OpenAI said on Nov. 25 that an internal artificial intelligence model had established a theoretical speed limit for multiplying matrices, a question that had occupied mathematicians and computer scientists for more than half a century [thehindu.com#1]. The previous week, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis [thehindu.com#1][npr.org#1].

The Riemann proof is encoded in more than 17 million lines of Lean, a proof-checking language. Human review continues, and a mathematician interviewed by NPR said the code passed checks despite its scale [indianexpress.com#1][npr.org#1]. Some mathematicians warn that mass-producing results could strain research and education; others say AI lets them explore unfamiliar mathematical techniques more quickly [zmescience.com#1][forskning.no#1].
quote: Even though I have no understanding of the proof, and nobody does, I am more confident that this proof is correct than any proof I have ever encountered.
quote_author: Andrew Sutherland, MIT mathematician specializing in Lean
talking_points: Cost of AI-generated results: OpenAI estimated that finding its Navier-Stokes solution cost $15 million, leaving a potential $14 million net loss even if it received the Clay Institute prize [zmescience.com#1].

perspectives.text: Kurusch Ebrahimi-Fard, mathematics professor and researcher at Simula’s SURE-AI center: He said researchers should neither ignore, mystify nor demonize AI [forskning.no#1].

Thomas Surowiec, deputy head of Simula’s SURE-AI center: He said students who let AI do their thinking learn little and called for broad mathematical understanding and skepticism when using the tools [forskning.no#1].
Association for Human Mathematics: Its members have committed to AI-free research that prioritizes human thinking and judgment in the mathematical sciences [zmescience.com#1].

title: Global temperatures exceed pre-industrial average by 2°C for a week as El Niño intensifies
summary:
Preliminary data from Copernicus, the European Union’s climate-monitoring service, show global temperatures stayed more than 2°C above the 1850–1900 average for seven consecutive days, reaching 2.25°C above that baseline on Monday [ft.com#1]. These daily readings do not establish that the Paris Agreement’s temperature limit has been breached: that target is assessed over at least 20 years [ft.com#1]. Scientists attribute the spike to long-term human-caused warming combined with a strong El Niño [ft.com#1][theconversation.com#1].

The record run coincided with COP31 climate negotiations in Turkey, where nearly 200 countries failed to agree on language about moving away from fossil fuels [ft.com#1]. The UK Met Office forecasts an unusually sharp rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide in 2027 as drought weakens natural carbon sinks; one estimate puts the year-to-year increase at about 3.5 parts per million [ft.com#1][stirileprotv.ro#1]. The current El Niño began in June and is expected to continue until at least March [ft.com#1].
quote: El Niño will come and go; the underlying warming from greenhouse gas emissions will not, unless we bring those emissions down.
quote_author: Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for Climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts
talking_points: Autumn records: October 2026 was the warmest October worldwide since records began, while Toronto set an October heat record dating back 80 years [dw.com#1].
Pacific conditions: The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration put the chance of a historic El Niño event by January at 60% [ft.com#1].
Coastal hazards: Storms prompted flood warnings along the California coast and as far north as Oregon and Washington; New York postponed its Thanksgiving Day parade until Saturday [ft.com#1].

Emissions trajectory: A climate researcher writing for The Conversation said global emissions may have peaked in 2026, but stressed that a peak does not amount to the steep cuts needed to reduce warming [theconversation.com#1].

perspectives.text: Samantha Burgess, climate strategic lead at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, said governments face two tasks: preparing communities for higher temperatures and accelerating cuts in greenhouse gas emissions. She cited heat-related damage to roads and railways and pressure on hospitals [stirileprotv.ro#1].

Richard Betts, head of climate impacts research at the Met Office Hadley Centre, warned that drought in regions such as the Amazon can increase wildfire risks, harm ecosystems and threaten food and water supplies [stirileprotv.ro#1].

title: Researchers identify possible largest known scorpion, over one meter long
summary:
Researchers have identified Praearcturus gigas, a scorpion known from a fossil found in the United Kingdom dating to about 415 million years ago, as a candidate for the largest known scorpion. They estimated that the animal exceeded one meter in length. A new analysis combining CT scans with traditional fossil tracings resolved decades of uncertainty over its classification [sciencealert.com#1][stirileprotv.ro#1][unian.ua#1].

Paleontologist Richie Howard and colleagues infer that it hunted both on land and in water; terrestrial ecosystems were still developing at the time [sciencealert.com#1][skynewsarabia.com#1]. The researchers suggest that the absence of other large predators may have enabled its large size, while later competition may have contributed to its decline [sciencealert.com#1][unian.ua#1].
quote: If this is the case, then Praearcturus is an example of an animal that likely returned to the water after its ancestors moved onto land.
quote_author: Greg Edgecombe, paleontologist at the Natural History Museum in the UK
talking_points: Large pincers: Its pincers measured about 16 centimeters, longer than the bodies of many scorpion species alive today [sciencealert.com#1][unian.ua#1].
Possible sound: Ridge patterns on a limb may indicate stridulation—sound production by rubbing body parts together, a behavior used by some modern scorpions [sciencealert.com#1][stirileprotv.ro#1].

Fossil comparison: The team compared the British fossils with Canadian specimens of the ancient scorpion Eramoscorpius to place P. gigas within the scorpion family tree [sciencealert.com#1][unian.ua#1].

title: Trump proposes tariffs on 14 partners; China rate could reach 40%
summary:
The Trump administration proposed new tariffs on imports from 14 major trading partners, citing excess manufacturing capacity after a U.S. Supreme Court ruling in February struck down much of President Donald Trump’s earlier broad-based tariff program. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the countries’ manufacturing policies burden or restrict U.S. commerce; the proposed duties would rely on a different legal authority, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 [abcnews.com#1][time.com#1]. A separate proposal targets Brazilian sugar and finished aircraft, including a 10% duty on aircraft [time.com#1].

China faces a proposed 20% rate that Washington says could rise to 40% if Beijing does not adequately engage. Vietnam could face up to 35%, while several other proposed rates are subject to caps or reductions tied to trade agreements [cnbc.com#1][abcnews.com#1]. The proposals drew objections from China, Japan, Singapore, the European Union and Brazil, among others [abcnews.com#1][time.com#1].

The duties are not final: affected parties can submit comments, and a hearing is scheduled for Jan. 25. Final tariffs are expected as early as February or March. Economist Stephen Brown of Capital Economics said the new measures would largely replace earlier tariffs but could still keep core goods inflation firm into next year [theguardian.com#1][scmp.com#1][mprnews.org#1].
quote: China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests.
quote_author: He Yadong, spokesperson for China’s Ministry of Commerce
talking_points: China exemptions: The U.S. proposal exempts about $30 billion of Chinese goods covered by reciprocal tariff cuts [scmp.com#1][manilatimes.net#1].
Singapore trade: Singapore says the U.S. has run a trade surplus with the city-state for more than 20 years; under their free-trade agreement, Singapore imposes no tariffs on U.S. goods [cnbc.com#1].
Investigation scope: The U.S. probe covered sectors including steel, aluminum, automobiles, batteries, chemicals, electronics, semiconductors, solar modules and shipbuilding [firstpost.com#1].
Brazilian exports: Brazil said it had negotiated in good faith with Washington on the Section 301 matter for more than a year before objecting to the new proposal [time.com#1].

Market response: After the announcement, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.25%; WisdomTree research director Aneeka Gupta cited renewed uncertainty over technology investment plans [cgtn.com#1].

perspectives.text: Trump administration: Greer said the measures are intended to level the playing field for U.S. workers and respond to market-distorting practices that he said weaken U.S. manufacturing [time.com#1].

China’s Ministry of Commerce: Spokesperson He Yadong argued the tariffs would disrupt supply chains, raise inflation and harm businesses and consumers, and called for negotiations rather than unilateral measures [scmp.com#1].
Brazilian government: Brasília said it would continue negotiating but would not rule out retaliatory measures against what it called an unacceptable unilateral action [theguardian.com#1].

title: Denny’s restores Nvidia founder plaque as Huang returns to CEO role
summary:
Denny’s publicly welcomed Jensen Huang back as Nvidia’s chief executive and said it had restored a plaque marking the San Jose diner booth where Huang and co-founders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem discussed starting the chipmaker [cnbc.com#1][businessinsider.com#1]. The restaurant chain said it learned the plaque had been removed on Nov. 13, one day after Huang resigned, and put it back shortly afterward. It has not said who removed it or why [seattletimes.com#1][mashable.com#1].

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang on Nov. 23, 11 days after accepting his resignation following reports of an affair with a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a customer suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. Huang acknowledged infidelity; Nvidia’s independent board review is continuing [nbcbayarea.com#1][ft.com#1][foxbusiness.com#1]. The board said it considered input from senior U.S. government officials, while President Donald Trump has said he helped secure Huang’s return [nbcbayarea.com#1][watson.ch#1].

Denny’s posted its renewed tribute on Nov. 25. The endorsement drew online mockery and criticism. Huang’s reinstatement also renewed questions about Nvidia’s succession planning, board independence and oversight of export-control compliance [businessinsider.com#1][nbcbayarea.com#1][ft.com#1].
quote: a better CEO the second time around
quote_author: Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive
talking_points: Online response: Business Insider reported that Denny’s post had drawn more than 3.9 million views on X, with commenters divided between jokes and criticism of the chain’s support for Huang [businessinsider.com#1].
Board scrutiny: Four Nvidia directors joined the board in 1993 or 1997, and governance experts questioned whether long-serving directors can remain independent [nbcbayarea.com#1].
Compliance changes: Nvidia’s board said it would appoint a chief compliance officer and created a committee to oversee national security and export controls [ft.com#1].
Credit risk: S&P Global Ratings warned it could cut Nvidia’s AA issuer rating by one notch if the company does not address governance deficiencies [ft.com#1].
Leadership structure: Huang defended a flat structure in which dozens of senior executives report directly to him [ft.com#1].

perspectives.text: Denny’s: The chain says Huang’s personal history with it began when he worked there as a teenager, and that Nvidia’s origin story is part of Denny’s history worth preserving [seattletimes.com#1][cnbc.com#1].

Kathleen Day, Johns Hopkins Carey Business School lecturer: Day said shareholders should demand a new board, arguing directors must represent shareholders rather than the chief executive [nbcbayarea.com#1].
